concerns.message: The fix only batches *free* triggers (losses, replacements, boundary carryover). Targeted rumors, the third sighting trigger in intel-core/intel-task.md, are left out. But the required property checker says "any two sighting-needing triggers of one player within the same step are delivered in the same message", and a paid targeted request is a sighting-needing trigger. The task never says how a targeted request on the same tick as a loss or replacement interacts with the single end-of-step flush. If the targeted request is handled first and delivers a sighting, it uses up the snapshot's cap, and the same-tick loss type is deferred for up to a whole interval. That is the exact symptom this run exists to remove. If the targeted request is handled after the flush, it gets `capped` even though a sighting went out that same tick.
concerns.consequence: There are two likely outcomes. (a) The worker writes the checker literally, and it fails on seeds where a targeted request and a loss coincide, burning verification attempts. (b) The worker quietly narrows the checker to free triggers, and the next general reviewer blocks the run a third time on the same late-second-type symptom through the targeted path. Settle it before the worker starts. The simplest rule: a targeted request adds its type to the same per-step accumulator. Its outcome is `sighting` if the single end-of-step message goes out, or `capped` if it doesn't. A capped paid type is never queued as pending, so it is never charged for something deferred.

concerns.message: The property checker has to know which triggers of a player happened within one step, including replacement triggers. Those come from the module's internal journal staleness, not only from the world-view diff. Deriving them outside the step means re-implementing staleness and 'every remaining copy is carried' in the checker. The shortcut is to have `stepIntel` expose trigger information, but that changes the settled step shape `{ state, messages, outcomes }` and breaks 'keep the structure'.
concerns.consequence: Either a checker that re-derives journal logic, which is large and can hide shared bugs, or an API change a reviewer will flag. Recommend deriving losses from held-type diffs and replacements from the stale messages already emitted in the same step, which are observable output, without changing the return shape.

concerns.message: "Flush once at the end of the player's step" assumes each player's losses, replacements and boundary carryover are handled in one per-player block. If the snapshot runs a global pass (for example, all losses, then a journal staleness pass over all rumors, then a boundary flush), there is no single 'end of the player's step'. The flush must go after every pass, keyed by player. I could not verify this myself, because the snapshot (`2309421`) is only reachable through a git ref that this read-only challenge can't open.
concerns.consequence: A worker who puts the flush at the end of the first per-player loop still splits a replacement triggered in a later pass into a second message or a deferral. The new scripted test 'a loss plus a replacement on one tick produce one message' catches it only if the scenario has both triggers need a sighting at once.

concerns.message: Finding 2 drops the starting rumor for a type whose every copy is carried. The PRD (§2 Spawn fairness) promises every player 'a rumor leading toward a reachable objective'. The motivating late-joiner case can't happen under the PRD: late arrivals wait in the lobby, and at control start every rubbing is sealed at a source (§4). So the change is harmless in real matches, but a player whose every missing type is carried gets zero starting leads, and no later trigger ever gives them one for that type.
concerns.consequence: Nothing breaks in real matches. But a reviewer reading §2 may flag 'a player with no starting rumor' as a spec violation. Have docs/intel.md state that this case is unreachable under §2 and §4, and that the choice is deliberate.

concerns.message: Batching changes when, and in what order, sighting construction runs within a step. If choosing a carrier sector or the message's type order uses the seeded generator or the iteration order, existing seed-pinned scripted expectations and any golden `hashState` values may shift, not only the tests the task names.
concerns.consequence: The worker changes more existing expectations than the task authorizes. Each has to be listed in the report, or reviewers will read it as unexplained test churn. Emitting types in a fixed order (the preset's type order) inside a message keeps it deterministic and easy to review.

simpler_alternative: Give each player one sighting accumulator per step, a sorted set of types. It starts with the player's pending set if a boundary was crossed. Losses, replacements and targeted requests all add to it, and none of them calls the flush themselves. After every pass of the step, each player gets exactly one decision. If the cap allows (or it's minute 28 or later), emit one message listing every still-eligible type from the older snapshot, and answer each targeted request in it `sighting`. Otherwise keep the free types as the single pending set, and answer targeted requests `capped`. This replaces the per-type `freeLead` → `flushPending` calls with one emit point. It makes 'same step ⇒ same message' true by construction for all three triggers, and the checker reduces to 'at most one sighting message per player per step'.
cheap_experiment: After restoring `2309421`, read where `stepIntel` handles targeted requests relative to the per-player loss/replacement code and the boundary flush in `step.ts` (around lines 380–440). Then add one scripted test before changing anything: a player with the cap available loses type A (every other copy carried) and buys a targeted rumor for type B (every copy carried) on the same tick. If the two types come out in two messages, or B gets `capped` while A is delivered, the operator needs to add targeted requests to the batching rule before the fix is written. If they already share one message, concern 1 drops to P2.
